questions.q: Which command should you run first to diagnose a "no default Dev Hub found" error?
options: sf project deploy preview
sf org list
sf package version create list
sf data export tree
questions.explain: sf org list immediately shows which of the three causes you're dealing with: no Dev Hub-flagged org authenticated at all, or one present but not marked default.

questions.q: What are the three real causes this lesson names behind a "no default Dev Hub" error?
options: A corrupted sfdx-project.json, a missing .forceignore, and an expired scratch org
A missing Apex test, a failed code-coverage check, and a namespace conflict
An outdated API version, a missing package.xml, and a broken VS Code extension
Dev Hub never enabled in the org, the CLI never authenticated to it, or an org authenticated but never set as default (with --target-dev-hub not passed)
questions.explain: The three causes are: Dev Hub was never enabled in Setup, the CLI was never authenticated to that org, or an org is authenticated but not marked default and --target-dev-hub wasn't passed explicitly.

questions.q: When a file mysteriously isn't deploying, what does this lesson recommend checking first, before assuming the deploy command is broken?
options: Whether the Dev Hub is enabled
Whether the scratch org has expired
.forceignore, using sf project deploy preview to see exactly what's being excluded
Whether a managed package is installed
questions.explain: A loosely written .forceignore glob pattern can silently exclude more than intended; sf project deploy preview explicitly lists what's being ignored, immediately distinguishing a forceignore issue from an actual deploy bug.

questions.q: What is the real fix when scratch org creation fails because the Dev Hub has hit its active scratch org allocation limit?
options: Actually deleting scratch orgs you're done with, rather than leaving unused ones sitting around until they expire naturally
Passing a special --force flag to override the limit
Switching to a different metadata API version
Re-registering the Dev Hub's namespace
questions.explain: The fix isn't a CLI flag — it's actively deleting scratch orgs you're finished with (sf org delete scratch) instead of letting unused ones accumulate against the Dev Hub's active allocation limit.

questions.q: If a specific metadata type behaves unexpectedly during retrieve or deploy — appearing missing or only partially captured — what should you check before assuming your project is misconfigured?
options: Your Git commit history
Salesforce's published Metadata Coverage Report, which documents type-specific retrieve/deploy support limitations
The scratch org's duration-days setting
The CLI's installed plugin list
questions.explain: Some metadata types are retrieve-only or only partially supported — a documented platform limitation tracked in the Metadata Coverage Report, not a misconfiguration in your project.
